plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem topped by a broad flower head made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark disc of tiny florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky. It is grown as an ornamental and as an oil and seed crop, and it also grows wild in open areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray, narrow leaves and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. It is grown in gardens and on large commercial fields for essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, with peak bloom in July and into August
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely derives from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial whose large, round leaves and showy, fragrant flowers rise on stalks above the water surface. The leaves repel water and dirt. The flowers open in the morning and close by afternoon over a few days. It is rooted in muddy pond and wetland bottoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking from June to August
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in China, India, Japan, Vietnam, and in water gardens around the world
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been known to germinate after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the leaf's self-cleaning surface inspired the term 'lotus effect' in materials science.

plants.name: Chamaenerion angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower producing long spikes of vivid magenta-pink flowers that bloom from the bottom of the spike upward. It rapidly colonizes burned or disturbed land, often forming sweeping carpets of color. The seeds bear silky fluff that disperses on the wind.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer (July to September)
plants.location: Circumpolar across the Northern Hemisphere, including Alaska, Canada, northern Europe, Siberia, and mountainous regions
plants.funFact: Fireweed is often among the first plants to reappear after wildfires, and the progress of blooming up the spike is said to signal the approaching end of summer.
